\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{افزایش} (afzâyesh)}{افزایش (afzâyesh)}]{\fa{افزایش} (afzâyesh) — an increase, a rise}

\label{lesson:FA-C373-afzayesh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to give rise to, then the Persian for a reaction.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{افزایش}}
\textbf{\fa{افزایش}} (\emph{afzâyesh}) — \textquotedblleft{}an increase, a rise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{افزایش} \fa{قیمت} \fa{نان} \fa{همه} \fa{را} \fa{نگران} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{afzâyesh-e qeymat-e nân hame râ negarân kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The rise in the price of bread worried everyone.
\end{quote}

From \emph{afzâ-}, the present stem of \emph{afzudan} \textquotedblleft{}to add, to increase\textquotedblright{}. The opposite is \emph{kâhesh}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{افزایش}} is native Persian, built on \emph{afzâ-}, the present stem of \emph{afzudan} \textquotedblleft{}to add, to increase\textquotedblright{}, with the noun suffix \emph{-yesh}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{afzâyesh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{afzâyesh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{afzâyesh}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to give rise to, then the Persian for a reaction, then say \emph{afzâyesh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{افزایش} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An increase, a rise\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{افزایش} \fa{یافتن} (afzâyesh yâftan)}{افزایش یافتن (afzâyesh yâftan)}]{\fa{افزایش} \fa{یافتن} (afzâyesh yâftan) — to increase, to go up}

\label{lesson:FA-C373-afzayesh-yaftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a reaction, then the Persian for an increase.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{افزایش} \fa{یافتن}}
\textbf{\fa{افزایش} \fa{یافتن}} (\emph{afzâyesh yâftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to increase, to go up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{تعداد} \fa{دانشجوها} \fa{هر} \fa{سال} \fa{افزایش} \fa{مییابد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{te'dâd-e dâneshjuhâ har sâl afzâyesh miyâbad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The number of students goes up every year.
\end{quote}

Formal; \emph{yâftan} \textquotedblleft{}to find\textquotedblright{} has the present stem \emph{yâb-}. In speech, \emph{ziyâd shodan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{افزایش} \fa{یافتن}} is native Persian, built from \emph{afzâyesh} \textquotedblleft{}increase\textquotedblright{} with \emph{yâftan} \textquotedblleft{}to find\textquotedblright{}, which in formal Persian turns a noun of change into a verb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{afzâyesh yâftan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{afzâyesh yâftan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{afzâyesh yâftan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a reaction, then the Persian for an increase, then say \emph{afzâyesh yâftan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{افزایش} \fa{یافتن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To increase, to go up\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کاهش} (kâhesh)}{کاهش (kâhesh)}]{\fa{کاهش} (kâhesh) — a decrease, a reduction}

\label{lesson:FA-C373-kahesh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an increase, then the Persian for to increase.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کاهش}}
\textbf{\fa{کاهش}} (\emph{kâhesh}) — \textquotedblleft{}a decrease, a reduction\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{کاهش} \fa{باران} \fa{برای} \fa{کشاورزها} \fa{مشکل} \fa{بزرگی} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kâhesh-e bârân barâye keshâvarzhâ moshkel-e bozorgi ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Less rain is a big problem for farmers.
\end{quote}

From \emph{kâh-}, the present stem of \emph{kâstan} \textquotedblleft{}to lessen\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Kâhesh yâftan} — to decrease.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{کاهش}} is native Persian, built on \emph{kâh-}, the present stem of \emph{kâstan} \textquotedblleft{}to lessen, to reduce\textquotedblright{}, with the noun suffix \emph{-esh}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kâhesh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kâhesh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{kâhesh}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for an increase, then the Persian for to increase, then say \emph{kâhesh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{کاهش} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A decrease, a reduction\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کاهش} \fa{دادن} (kâhesh dâdan)}{کاهش دادن (kâhesh dâdan)}]{\fa{کاهش} \fa{دادن} (kâhesh dâdan) — to reduce, to cut}

\label{lesson:FA-C373-kahesh-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to increase, then the Persian for a decrease.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کاهش} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{کاهش} \fa{دادن}} (\emph{kâhesh dâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to reduce, to cut\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{شرکت} \fa{ساعت} \fa{کار} \fa{را} \fa{کاهش} \fa{داد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sherkat sâ'at-e kâr râ kâhesh dâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The company cut working hours.
\end{quote}

\emph{Kâhesh} + \emph{dâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{} (present stem \emph{deh-}). The object takes \emph{râ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{کاهش} \fa{دادن}} is native Persian, built from \emph{kâhesh} \textquotedblleft{}decrease\textquotedblright{} with \emph{dâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}, which EtymDB traces to PIE \emph{deh\textsubscript{3}-} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kâhesh dâdan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kâhesh dâdan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{kâhesh dâdan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to increase, then the Persian for a decrease, then say \emph{kâhesh dâdan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{کاهش} \fa{دادن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To reduce, to cut\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{رشد} \fa{کردن} (roshd kardan)}{رشد کردن (roshd kardan)}]{\fa{رشد} \fa{کردن} (roshd kardan) — to grow}

\label{lesson:FA-C373-roshd-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a decrease, then the Persian for to reduce.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{رشد} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{رشد} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{roshd kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to grow\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{شهر} \fa{در} \fa{ده} \fa{سال} \fa{گذشته} \fa{خیلی} \fa{رشد} \fa{کرده} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in shahr dar dah sâl-e gozashte kheyli roshd karde ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This city has grown a lot in the last ten years.
\end{quote}

\emph{Roshd} \textquotedblleft{}growth\textquotedblright{} + \emph{kardan}. For people, plants, cities and economies.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{رشد}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{rushd} (EtymDB), a word usually glossed as maturity or right guidance; in Persian it means growth.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{roshd kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{roshd kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a decrease, then the Persian for to reduce, then say \emph{roshd kardan} again
\end{itemize}
